barbarian.name: Rage
barbarian.summary: You can imbue yourself with a primal power called Rage, a force that grants you extraordinary might and resilience. You can enter it as a Bonus Action if you aren’t wearing Heavy armor.

barbarian.name: Unarmored Defense
barbarian.summary: While you aren’t wearing any armor, your base Armor Class equals 10 plus your Dexterity and Constitution modifiers. You can use a Shield and still gain this benefit.

barbarian.name: Weapon Mastery
barbarian.summary: Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of Simple or Martial Melee weapons of your choice, such as Greataxes and Handaxes.

barbarian.name: Danger Sense
barbarian.summary: You gain an uncanny sense of when things aren’t as they should be, giving you an edge when you dodge perils. You have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws unless you have the Incapacitated condition.

barbarian.name: Reckless Attack
barbarian.summary: You can throw aside all concern for defense to attack with increased ferocity. When you make your first attack roll on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly.

barbarian.name: Barbarian Subclass
barbarian.summary: You gain a Barbarian subclass of your choice. The Path of the Berserker subclass is detailed after this class’s description. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Barbarian levels.

barbarian.name: Primal Knowledge
barbarian.summary: You gain proficiency in another skill of your choice from the skill list available to Barbarians at level 1. In addition, while your Rage is active, you can channel primal power when you attempt certain tasks; whenever you make an ability check using one of the following skills, you can make it as a Strength check even if it normally uses a different ability: Acrobatics, Intimidation, Perception, Stealth, or Survival.

barbarian.name: Ability Score Improvement
barbarian.summary: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see “Feats”) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Barbarian levels 8, 12, and 16.

barbarian.name: Extra Attack
barbarian.summary: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

barbarian.name: Fast Movement
barbarian.summary: Your speed increases by 10 feet while you aren’t wearing Heavy armor.

barbarian.name: Feral Instinct
barbarian.summary: Your instincts are so honed that you have Advantage on Initiative rolls.

barbarian.name: Instinctive Pounce
barbarian.summary: As part of the Bonus Action you take to enter your Rage, you can move up to half your Speed.

barbarian.name: Brutal Strike
barbarian.summary: If you use Reckless Attack, you can forgo any Advantage on one Strength-based attack roll of your choice on your turn. The chosen attack roll mustn’t have Disadvantage.

barbarian.name: Relentless Rage
barbarian.summary: Your Rage can keep you fighting despite grievous wounds. If you drop to 0 Hit Points while your Rage is active and don’t die outright, you can make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw.

barbarian.name: Improved Brutal Strike
barbarian.summary: You have honed new ways to attack furiously. The following effects are now among your Brutal Strike options. Staggering Blow. The target has Disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes, and it can’t make Opportunity Attacks until the start of your next turn.

barbarian.name: Persistent Rage
barbarian.summary: When you roll Initiative, you can regain all expended uses of Rage. After you regain uses of Rage in this way, you can’t do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

barbarian.name: Improved Brutal Strike
barbarian.summary: The extra damage of your Brutal Strike increases to 2d10. In addition, you can use two different Brutal Strike effects whenever you use your Brutal Strike feature.

barbarian.name: Indomitable Might
barbarian.summary: If your total for a Strength check or Strength saving throw is less than your Strength score, you can use that score in place of the total.

barbarian.name: Epic Boon
barbarian.summary: You gain an Epic Boon feat (see “Feats”) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Irresistible Offense is recommended.

barbarian.name: Primal Champion
barbarian.summary: You embody primal power. Your Strength and Constitution scores increase by 4, to a maximum of 25.

bard.name: Bardic Inspiration
bard.summary: You can supernaturally inspire others through words, music, or dance. This inspiration is represented by your Bardic Inspiration die, which is a d6. Using Bardic Inspiration.

bard.name: Spellcasting
bard.summary: You have learned to cast spells through your bardic arts. See “Spells” for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Bard spells, which appear in the Bard spell list later in the class’s description.

bard.name: Expertise
bard.summary: You gain Expertise (see “Rules Glossary”) in two of your skill proficiencies of your choice. Performance and Persuasion are recommended if you have proficiency in them.

bard.name: Jack of All Trades
bard.summary: You can add half your Proficiency Bonus (round down) to any ability check you make that uses a skill proficiency you lack and that doesn’t otherwise use your Proficiency Bonus.

bard.name: Bard Subclass
bard.summary: You gain a Bard subclass of your choice. The College of Lore subclass is detailed after this class’s description. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Bard levels.

bard.name: Ability Score Improvement
bard.summary: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see “Feats”) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Bard levels 8, 12, and 16.

bard.name: Font of Inspiration
bard.summary: You now regain all your expended uses of Bardic Inspiration when you finish a Short or Long Rest. In addition, you can expend a spell slot (no action required) to regain one expended use of Bardic Inspiration.

bard.name: Countercharm
bard.summary: You can use musical notes or words of power to disrupt mind-influencing effects. If you or a creature within 30 feet of you fails a saving throw against an effect that applies the Charmed or Frightened condition, you can take a Reaction to cause the save to be rerolled, and the new roll has Advantage.

bard.name: Magical Secrets
bard.summary: You’ve learned secrets from various magical traditions. Whenever you reach a Bard level (including this level) and the Prepared Spells number in the Bard Features table increases, you can choose any of your new prepared spells from the Bard, Cleric, Druid, and Wizard spell lists, and the chosen spells count as Bard spells for you (see a class’s section for its spell list).

bard.name: Superior Inspiration
bard.summary: When you roll Initiative, you regain expended uses of Bardic Inspiration until you have two if you have fewer than that.

bard.name: Epic Boon
bard.summary: You gain an Epic Boon feat (see “Feats”) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Spell Recall is recommended.

bard.name: Words of Creation
bard.summary: You have mastered two of the Words of Creation: the words of life and death. You therefore always have the Power Word Heal and Power Word Kill spells prepared. When you cast either spell, you can target a second creature with it if that creature is within 10 feet of the first target.

cleric.name: Spellcasting
cleric.summary: You have learned to cast spells through prayer and meditation. See “Spells” for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Cleric spells, which appear on the Cleric spell list later in the class’s description.

cleric.name: Divine Order
cleric.summary: You have dedicated yourself to one of the following sacred roles of your choice. Protector. Trained for battle, you gain proficiency with Martial weapons and training with Heavy armor.

cleric.name: Channel Divinity
cleric.summary: You can channel divine energy directly from the Outer Planes to fuel magical effects. You start with two such effects: Divine Spark and Turn Undead, each of which is described below.

cleric.name: Cleric Subclass
cleric.summary: You gain a Cleric subclass of your choice. The Life Domain subclass is detailed after this class’s description. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Cleric levels.

cleric.name: Ability Score Improvement
cleric.summary: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see “Feats”) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Cleric levels 8, 12, and 16.

cleric.name: Sear Undead
cleric.summary: Whenever you use Turn Undead, you can roll a number of d8s equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1d8) and add the rolls together. Each Undead that fails its saving throw against that use of Turn Undead takes Radiant damage equal to the roll’s total.

cleric.name: Blessed Strikes
cleric.summary: Divine power infuses you in battle. You gain one of the following options of your choice (if you get either option from a Cleric subclass in an older book, use only the option you choose for this feature).

cleric.name: Divine Intervention
cleric.summary: You can call on your deity or pantheon to intervene on your behalf. As a Magic action, choose any Cleric spell of level 5 or lower that doesn’t require a Reaction to cast.

cleric.name: Improved Blessed Strikes
cleric.summary: The option you chose for Blessed Strikes grows more powerful. Divine Strike. The extra damage of your Divine Strike increases to 2d8. Potent Spellcasting. When you cast a Cleric cantrip and deal damage to a creature with it, you can give vitality to yourself or another creature within 60 feet of yourself, granting a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to twice your Wisdom modifier.

cleric.name: Epic Boon
cleric.summary: You gain an Epic Boon feat (see “Feats”) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Fate is recommended.

cleric.name: Greater Divine Intervention
cleric.summary: You can call on even more powerful divine intervention. When you use your Divine Intervention feature, you can choose Wish when you select a spell. If you do so, you can’t use Divine Intervention again until you finish 2d4 Long Rests.

druid.name: Spellcasting
druid.summary: You have learned to cast spells through studying the mystical forces of nature. See “Spells” for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details

druid.name: Druidic
druid.summary: You know Druidic, the secret language of Druids. While learning this ancient tongue, you also unlocked the magic of communicating with animals; you always have the Speak with Animals spell prepared.

druid.name: Primal Order
druid.summary: You have dedicated yourself to one of the following sacred roles of your choice. Magician. You know one extra cantrip from the Druid spell list. In addition, your mystical connection to nature gives you a bonus to your Intelligence (Arcana or Nature) checks.

druid.name: Wild Shape
druid.summary: The power of nature allows you to assume the form of an animal. As a Bonus Action, you shape-shift into a Beast form that you have learned for this feature (see “Known Forms” below).

druid.name: Wild Companion
druid.summary: You can summon a nature spirit that assumes an animal form to aid you. As a Magic action, you can expend a spell slot or a use of Wild Shape to cast the Find Familiar spell without Material components.

druid.name: Druid Subclass
druid.summary: You gain a Druid subclass of your choice. The Circle of the Land subclass is detailed after this class’s description. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Druid levels.

druid.name: Ability Score Improvement
druid.summary: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see “Feats”) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Druid levels 8, 12, and 16.

druid.name: Wild Resurgence
druid.summary: Once on each of your turns, if you have no uses of Wild Shape left, you can give yourself one use by expending a spell slot (no action required). In addition, you can expend one use of Wild Shape (no action required) to give yourself a level 1 spell slot, but you can’t do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

druid.name: Elemental Fury
druid.summary: The might of the elements flows through you. You gain one of the following options of your choice. Potent Spellcasting. Add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any Druid cantrip.

druid.name: Improved Elemental Fury
druid.summary: The option you chose for Elemental Fury grows more powerful, as detailed below. Potent Spellcasting. When you cast a Druid cantrip with a range of 10 feet or greater, the spell’s range increases by 300 feet.

druid.name: Beast Spells
druid.summary: While using Wild Shape, you can cast spells in Beast form, except for any spell that has a Material component with a cost specified or that consumes its Material component.

druid.name: Epic Boon
druid.summary: You gain an Epic Boon feat (see “Feats”) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Dimensional Travel is recommended.

druid.name: Archdruid
druid.summary: The vitality of nature constantly blooms within you, granting you the following benefits. Evergreen Wild Shape. Whenever you roll Initiative and have no uses of Wild Shape left, you regain one expended use of it.

fighter.name: Fighting Style
fighter.summary: You have honed your martial prowess and gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice (see “Feats”). Defense is recommended. Whenever you gain a Fighter level, you can replace the feat you chose with a different Fighting Style feat.

fighter.name: Second Wind
fighter.summary: You have a limited well of physical and mental stamina that you can draw on. As a Bonus Action, you can use it to regain Hit Points equal to 1d10 plus your Fighter level.

fighter.name: Weapon Mastery
fighter.summary: Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of three kinds of Simple or Martial weapons of your choice. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices.

fighter.name: Action Surge
fighter.summary: You can push yourself beyond your normal limits for a moment. On your turn, you can take one additional action, except the Magic action. Once you use this feature, you can’t do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

fighter.name: Tactical Mind
fighter.summary: You have a mind for tactics on and off the battlefield. When you fail an ability check, you can expend a use of your Second Wind to push yourself toward success.

fighter.name: Fighter Subclass
fighter.summary: You gain a Fighter subclass of your choice. The Champion subclass is detailed after this class’s description. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Fighter levels.

fighter.name: Ability Score Improvement
fighter.summary: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see “Feats”) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Fighter levels 6, 8, 12, 14, and 16.

fighter.name: Extra Attack
fighter.summary: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

fighter.name: Tactical Shift
fighter.summary: Whenever you activate your Second Wind with a Bonus Action, you can move up to half your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

fighter.name: Indomitable
fighter.summary: If you fail a saving throw, you can reroll it with a bonus equal to your Fighter level. You must use the new roll, and you can’t use this feature again until you finish a Long Rest.

fighter.name: Tactical Master
fighter.summary: When you attack with a weapon whose mastery property you can use, you can replace that property with the Push, Sap, or Slow property for that attack.

fighter.name: Two Extra Attacks
fighter.summary: You can attack three times instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

fighter.name: Studied Attacks
fighter.summary: You study your opponents and learn from each attack you make. If you make an attack roll against a creature and miss, you have Advantage on your next attack roll against that creature before the end of your next turn.

fighter.name: Epic Boon
fighter.summary: You gain an Epic Boon feat (see “Feats”) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Combat Prowess is recommended.

fighter.name: Three Extra Attacks
fighter.summary: You can attack four times instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

monk.name: Martial Arts
monk.summary: Your practice of martial arts gives you mastery of combat styles that use your Unarmed Strike and Monk weapons, which are the following: • Simple Melee weapons • Martial Melee weapons that have the Light property You gain the following benefits while you are unarmed or wielding only Monk weapons and you aren’t wearing armor or wielding a Shield.

monk.name: Unarmored Defense
monk.summary: While you aren’t wearing armor or wielding a Shield, your base Armor Class equals 10 plus your Dexterity and Wisdom modifiers.

monk.name: Monk’s Focus
monk.summary: Your focus and martial training allow you to harness a well of extraordinary energy within yourself. This energy is represented by Focus Points. Your Monk level determines the number of points you have, as shown in the Focus Points column of the Monk Features table.

monk.name: Unarmored Movement
monk.summary: Your speed increases by 10 feet while you aren’t wearing armor or wielding a Shield. This bonus increases when you reach certain Monk levels, as shown on the Monk Features table.

monk.name: Uncanny Metabolism
monk.summary: When you roll Initiative, you can regain all expended Focus Points. When you do so, roll your Martial Arts die, and regain a number of Hit Points equal to your Monk level plus the number rolled.

monk.name: Deflect Attacks
monk.summary: When an attack roll hits you and its damage includes Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, you can take a Reaction to reduce the attack’s total damage against you.

monk.name: Monk Subclass
monk.summary: You gain a Monk subclass of your choice. The Warrior of the Open Hand subclass is detailed after this class’s description. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Monk levels.

monk.name: Ability Score Improvement
monk.summary: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see “Feats”) or another feat of your choice for which you

monk.name: Slow Fall
monk.summary: You can take a Reaction when you fall to reduce any damage you take from the fall by an amount equal to five times your Monk level.

monk.name: Extra Attack
monk.summary: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

monk.name: Stunning Strike
monk.summary: Once per turn when you hit a creature with a Monk weapon or an Unarmed Strike, you can expend 1 Focus Point to attempt a stunning strike. The target must make a Constitution saving throw.

monk.name: Empowered Strikes
monk.summary: Whenever you deal damage with your Unarmed Strike, it can deal your choice of Force damage or its normal damage type.

monk.name: Evasion
monk.summary: When you’re subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw and only half damage if you fail.

monk.name: Acrobatic Movement
monk.summary: While you aren’t wearing armor or wielding a Shield, you gain the ability to move along vertical surfaces and across liquids on your turn without falling during the movement.

monk.name: Heightened Focus
monk.summary: Your Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, and Step of the Wind gain the following benefits. Flurry of Blows. You can expend 1 Focus Point to use Flurry of Blows and make three Unarmed Strikes with it instead of two.

monk.name: Self-Restoration
monk.summary: Through sheer force of will, you can remove one of the following conditions from yourself at the end of each of your turns: Charmed, Frightened, or Poisoned. In addition, forgoing food and drink doesn’t give you levels of Exhaustion.

monk.name: Deflect Energy
monk.summary: You can now use your Deflect Attacks feature against attacks that deal any damage type, not just Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing.

monk.name: Disciplined Survivor
monk.summary: Your physical and mental discipline grant you proficiency in all saving throws. Additionally, whenever you make a saving throw and fail, you can expend 1 Focus Point to reroll it, and you must use the new roll.

monk.name: Perfect Focus
monk.summary: When you roll Initiative and don’t use Uncanny Metabolism, you regain expended Focus Points until you have 4 if you have 3 or fewer.

monk.name: Superior Defense
monk.summary: At the start of your turn, you can expend 3 Focus Points to bolster yourself against harm for 1 minute or until you have the Incapacitated condition. During that time, you have Resistance to all damage except Force damage.

monk.name: Epic Boon
monk.summary: You gain an Epic Boon feat (see “Feats”) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Irresistible Offense is recommended.

monk.name: Body and Mind
monk.summary: You have developed your body and mind to new heights. Your Dexterity and Wisdom scores increase by 4, to a maximum of 25.

paladin.name: Lay On Hands
paladin.summary: Your blessed touch can heal wounds. You have a pool of healing power that replenishes when you finish a Long Rest. With that pool, you can restore a total number of Hit Points equal to five times your Paladin level.

paladin.name: Spellcasting
paladin.summary: You have learned to cast spells through prayer and meditation. See “Spells” for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Paladin spells, which appear in the Paladin spell list later in the class’s description.

paladin.name: Weapon Mastery
paladin.summary: Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as Longswords and Javelins.

paladin.name: Fighting Style
paladin.summary: You gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice (see “Feats” for feats). Instead of choosing one of those feats, you can choose the option below. Blessed Warrior.

paladin.name: Paladin’s Smite
paladin.summary: You always have the Divine Smite spell prepared. In addition, you can cast it without expending a spell slot, but you must finish a Long Rest before you can cast it in this way again.

paladin.name: Channel Divinity
paladin.summary: You can channel divine energy directly from the Outer Planes, using it to fuel magical effects. You start with one such effect: Divine Sense, which is described below.

paladin.name: Paladin Subclass
paladin.summary: You gain a Paladin subclass of your choice. The Oath of Devotion subclass is detailed after this class’s description. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Paladin levels.

paladin.name: Ability Score Improvement
paladin.summary: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see “Feats”) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Paladin levels 8, 12, and 16.

paladin.name: Extra Attack
paladin.summary: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

paladin.name: Faithful Steed
paladin.summary: You can call on the aid of an otherworldly steed. You always have the Find Steed spell prepared. You can also cast the spell once without expending a spell slot, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a Long Rest.

paladin.name: Aura of Protection
paladin.summary: You radiate a protective, unseeable aura in a 10-foot Emanation that originates from you. The aura is inactive while you have the Incapacitated condition. You and your allies in the aura gain a bonus to saving throws equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum bonus of +1).

paladin.name: Abjure Foes
paladin.summary: As a Magic action, you can expend one use of this class’s Channel Divinity to overwhelm foes with awe. As you present your Holy Symbol or weapon, you can target a number of creatures equal to your

paladin.name: Aura of Courage
paladin.summary: You and your allies have Immunity to the Frightened condition while in your Aura of Protection. If a Frightened ally enters the aura, that condition has no effect on that ally while there.

paladin.name: Radiant Strikes
paladin.summary: Your strikes now carry supernatural power. When you hit a target with an attack roll using a Melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike, the target takes an extra 1d8 Radiant damage.

paladin.name: Restoring Touch
paladin.summary: When you use Lay On Hands on a creature, you can also remove one or more of the following conditions from the creature: Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Frightened, Paralyzed, or Stunned.

paladin.name: Aura Expansion
paladin.summary: Your Aura of Protection is now a 30-foot Emanation.

paladin.name: Epic Boon
paladin.summary: You gain an Epic Boon feat (see “Feats”) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Truesight is recommended.

ranger.name: Spellcasting
ranger.summary: You have learned to channel the magical essence of nature to cast spells. See “Spells” for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Ranger spells, which appear in the Ranger spell list later in the class’s description.

ranger.name: Favored Enemy
ranger.summary: You always have the Hunter’s Mark spell prepared. You can cast it twice without expending a spell slot, and you regain all expended uses of this ability when you finish a Long Rest.

ranger.name: Weapon Mastery
ranger.summary: Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your

ranger.name: Deft Explorer
ranger.summary: Thanks to your travels, you gain the following benefits. Expertise. Choose one of your skill proficiencies with which you lack Expertise. You gain Expertise in that skill.

ranger.name: Fighting Style
ranger.summary: You gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice (see “Feats”). Instead of choosing one of those feats, you can choose the option below. Druidic Warrior. You learn two Druid cantrips of your choice (see the Druid class’s section for a list of Druid spells).

ranger.name: Ranger Subclass
ranger.summary: You gain a Ranger subclass of your choice. The Hunter subclass is detailed after this class’s description. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Ranger levels.

ranger.name: Ability Score Improvement
ranger.summary: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see “Feats”) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Ranger levels 8, 12, and 16.

ranger.name: Extra Attack
ranger.summary: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

ranger.name: Roving
ranger.summary: Your Speed increases by 10 feet while you aren’t wearing Heavy armor. You also have a Climb Speed and a Swim Speed equal to your Speed.

ranger.name: Expertise
ranger.summary: Choose two of your skill proficiencies with which you lack Expertise. You gain Expertise in those skills.

ranger.name: Tireless
ranger.summary: Primal forces now help fuel you on your journeys, granting you the following benefits. Temporary Hit Points. As a Magic action, you can give yourself a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to 1d8 plus your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1).

ranger.name: Relentless Hunter
ranger.summary: Taking damage can’t break your Concentration on Hunter’s Mark.

ranger.name: Nature’s Veil
ranger.summary: You invoke spirits of nature to magically hide yourself. As a Bonus Action, you can give yourself the Invisible condition until the end of your next turn. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

ranger.name: Precise Hunter
ranger.summary: You have Advantage on attack rolls against the creature currently marked by your Hunter’s Mark.

ranger.name: Feral Senses
ranger.summary: Your connection to the forces of nature grants you Blindsight with a range of 30 feet.

ranger.name: Epic Boon
ranger.summary: You gain an Epic Boon feat (see “Feats”) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Dimensional Travel is recommended.

ranger.name: Foe Slayer
ranger.summary: The damage die of your Hunter’s Mark is a d10 rather than a d6.

rogue.name: Expertise
rogue.summary: You gain Expertise in two of your skill proficiencies of your choice. Sleight of Hand and Stealth are recommended if you have proficiency in them. At Rogue level 6, you gain Expertise in two more of your skill proficiencies of your choice.

rogue.name: Sneak Attack
rogue.summary: You know how to strike subtly and exploit a foe’s distraction. Once per turn, you can deal an extra 1d6 damage to one creature you hit with an attack

rogue.name: Thieves’ Cant
rogue.summary: You picked up various languages in the communities where you plied your roguish talents. You know Thieves’ Cant and one other language of your choice, which you choose from the language tables in “Character Creation.”

rogue.name: Weapon Mastery
rogue.summary: Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as Daggers and Shortbows.

rogue.name: Cunning Action
rogue.summary: Your quick thinking and agility allow you to move and act quickly. On your turn, you can take one of the following actions as a Bonus Action: Dash, Disengage, or Hide.

rogue.name: Rogue Subclass
rogue.summary: You gain a Rogue subclass of your choice. The Thief subclass is detailed after this class’s description. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Rogue levels.

rogue.name: Steady Aim
rogue.summary: As a Bonus Action, you give yourself Advantage on your next attack roll on the current turn. You can use this feature only if you haven’t moved during this turn, and after you use it, your Speed is 0 until the end of the current turn.

rogue.name: Ability Score Improvement
rogue.summary: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see “Feats”) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Rogue levels 8, 10, 12, and 16.

rogue.name: Cunning Strike
rogue.summary: You’ve developed cunning ways to use your Sneak Attack. When you deal Sneak Attack damage, you can add one of the following Cunning Strike effects. Each effect has a die cost, which is the number of Sneak Attack damage dice you must forgo to add the effect.

rogue.name: Uncanny Dodge
rogue.summary: When an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to halve the attack’s damage against you (round down).

rogue.name: Evasion
rogue.summary: You can nimbly dodge out of the way of certain dangers. When you’re subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw and only half damage if you fail.

rogue.name: Reliable Talent
rogue.summary: Whenever you make an ability check that uses one of your skill or tool proficiencies, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

rogue.name: Improved Cunning Strike
rogue.summary: You can use up to two Cunning Strike effects when you deal Sneak Attack damage, paying the die cost for each effect.

rogue.name: Devious Strikes
rogue.summary: You’ve practiced new ways to use your Sneak Attack deviously. The following effects are now among your Cunning Strike options. Daze (Cost: 2d6). The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw, or on its next turn, it can do only one of the following: move or take an action or a Bonus Action.

rogue.name: Slippery Mind
rogue.summary: Your cunning mind is exceptionally difficult to control. You gain proficiency in Wisdom and Charisma saving throws.

rogue.name: Elusive
rogue.summary: You’re so evasive that attackers rarely gain the upper hand against you. No attack roll can have Advantage against you unless you have the Incapacitated condition.

rogue.name: Epic Boon
rogue.summary: You gain an Epic Boon feat (see “Feats”) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of the Night Spirit is recommended.

rogue.name: Stroke of Luck
rogue.summary: You have a marvelous knack for succeeding when you need to. If you fail a D20 Test, you can turn the roll into a 20. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

sorcerer.name: Spellcasting
sorcerer.summary: Drawing from your innate magic, you can cast spells. See “Spells” for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Sorcerer spells, which appear in the Sorcerer spell list later in the class’s description.

sorcerer.name: Innate Sorcery
sorcerer.summary: An event in your past left an indelible mark on you, infusing you with simmering magic. As a Bonus Action, you can unleash that magic for 1 minute, during which you gain the following benefits:

sorcerer.name: Font of Magic
sorcerer.summary: You can tap into the wellspring of magic within yourself. This wellspring is represented by Sorcery Points, which allow you to create a variety of magical effects.

sorcerer.name: Metamagic
sorcerer.summary: Because your magic flows from within, you can alter your spells to suit your needs; you gain two Metamagic options of your choice from “Metamagic Options” later in this class’s description.

sorcerer.name: Sorcerer Subclass
sorcerer.summary: You gain a Sorcerer subclass of your choice. The Draconic Sorcery subclass is detailed after this class’s description. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Sorcerer levels.

sorcerer.name: Ability Score Improvement
sorcerer.summary: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see “Feats”) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Sorcerer levels 8, 12, and 16.

sorcerer.name: Sorcerous Restoration
sorcerer.summary: When you finish a Short Rest, you can regain expended Sorcery Points, but no more than a number equal to half your Sorcerer level (round down). Once you use this feature, you can’t do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

sorcerer.name: Sorcery Incarnate
sorcerer.summary: If you have no uses of Innate Sorcery left, you can use it if you spend 2 Sorcery Points when you take the Bonus Action to activate it. In addition, while your Innate Sorcery feature is active, you can use up to two of your Metamagic options on each spell you cast.

sorcerer.name: Epic Boon
sorcerer.summary: You gain an Epic Boon feat (see “Feats”) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Dimensional Travel is recommended.

sorcerer.name: Arcane Apotheosis
sorcerer.summary: While your Innate Sorcery feature is active, you can use one Metamagic option on each of your turns without spending Sorcery Points on it.

warlock.name: Eldritch Invocations
warlock.summary: You have unearthed Eldritch Invocations, pieces of forbidden knowledge that imbue you with an abiding magical ability or other lessons. You gain one invocation of your choice, such as Pact of the Tome.

warlock.name: Pact Magic
warlock.summary: Through occult ceremony, you have formed a pact with a mysterious entity to gain magical powers. The entity is a voice in the shadows—its identity unclear—but its boon to you is concrete: the ability to cast spells.

warlock.name: Magical Cunning
warlock.summary: You can perform an esoteric rite for 1 minute. At the end of it, you regain expended Pact Magic spell slots but no more than a number equal to half your maximum (round up).

warlock.name: Warlock Subclass
warlock.summary: You gain a Warlock subclass of your choice. The Fiend Patron subclass is detailed after this class’s description. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Warlock levels.

warlock.name: Ability Score Improvement
warlock.summary: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see “Feats”) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Warlock levels 8, 12, and 16.

warlock.name: Contact Patron
warlock.summary: In the past, you usually contacted your patron through intermediaries. Now you can communicate directly; you always have the Contact Other Plane spell prepared.

warlock.name: Mystic Arcanum
warlock.summary: Your patron grants you a magical secret called an arcanum. Choose one level 6 Warlock spell as this arcanum. You can cast your arcanum spell once without expending a spell slot, and you must finish a Long Rest before you can cast it in this way again.

warlock.name: Epic Boon
warlock.summary: You gain an Epic Boon feat (see “Feats”) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Fate is recommended.

warlock.name: Eldritch Master
warlock.summary: When you use your Magical Cunning feature, you regain all your expended Pact Magic spell slots.

wizard.name: Spellcasting
wizard.summary: As a student of arcane magic, you have learned to cast spells. See “Spells” for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Wizard spells, which appear in the Wizard spell list later in the class’s description.

wizard.name: Ritual Adept
wizard.summary: You can cast any spell as a Ritual if that spell has the Ritual tag and the spell is in your spellbook. You

wizard.name: Arcane Recovery
wizard.summary: You can regain some of your magical energy by studying your spellbook. When you finish a Short Rest, you can choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level equal to no more than half your Wizard level (round up), and none of the slots can be level 6 or higher.

wizard.name: Scholar
wizard.summary: While studying magic, you also specialized in another field of study. Choose one of the following skills in which you have proficiency: Arcana, History, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, or Religion.

wizard.name: Wizard Subclass
wizard.summary: You gain a Wizard subclass of your choice. The Evoker subclass is detailed after this class’s description. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Wizard levels.

wizard.name: Ability Score Improvement
wizard.summary: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see “Feats”) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Wizard levels 8, 12, and 16.

wizard.name: Memorize Spell
wizard.summary: Whenever you finish a Short Rest, you can study your spellbook and replace one of the level 1+ Wizard spells you have prepared for your Spellcasting feature with another level 1+ spell from the book.

wizard.name: Spell Mastery
wizard.summary: You have achieved such mastery over certain spells that you can cast them at will. Choose a level 1 and a level 2 spell in your spellbook that have a casting time of an action.

wizard.name: Epic Boon
wizard.summary: You gain an Epic Boon feat (see “Feats”) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Spell Recall is recommended.

wizard.name: Signature Spells
wizard.summary: Choose two level 3 spells in your spellbook as your signature spells. You always have these spells prepared, and you can cast each of them once at level 3 without expending a spell slot.
